html:
Most Albanians converted to Islam under Ottoman rule, mainly in the 1600s and 1700s, which made Albania one of the few Muslim majority countries in Europe.

Conversion brought lower taxes and careers in the Ottoman army and state, and Albanians rose high: several grand viziers, such as the Köprülü family, were of Albanian origin. Tirana was founded in 1614 around a mosque and a market. Catholics held on in the north and Orthodox Christians in the south, and the Sufi Bektashi order spread widely. Religious differences mattered less to Albanians than language and clan, which let the national movement unite Muslims and Christians. The Hoxha regime banned all religion in 1967.
sum: Most Albanians converted to Islam under Ottoman rule, mainly in the 1600s and 1700s, which made Albania one of the few Muslim majority countries in Europe.
